region.text: the north of Okinawa Island around Nakijin Castle

ledger.note: 1314: Hokuzan arises at Nakijin as one of the three kingdoms of Okinawa. 'Hokuzan first came into being in 1314 when Tamagusuku inherited the role of head chieftain' (infobox 'Established: 1314'); it lay 'in the north of Okinawa Island'. The page gives the districts, not an outline.
1416: Shō Hashi of Chūzan attacks Hokuzan. The page gives only the year and that Hashi conducted the attack after three anji vassals defected; no month.
1416: Nakijin Castle falls. 'Following a fierce defense, Nakijin castle fell, and the king and his closest vassals committed suicide.'

notes:
Written by Phase B agent jk-01-b on 2026-10-18 from three pages (budget 1-2: the Hokuzan page, plus two cross-checks for the 1416/1419 disagreement).

Disagreement between pages: the Hokuzan page (infobox and text) and the Ryukyu Kingdom page date the fall of Hokuzan to 1416; the Chūzan page says 1419 and the Nanzan page says Hashi took Nanzan 'ten years' after conquering Hokuzan (which implies 1419). The dossier follows 1416 (two pages, one of them the state's own). Cliopatria's Hokuzan row runs to 1421 and Chūzan's enlarged shape starts in 1422; both are later than any page.

The infobox gives no area; the Hokuzan page calls it the largest of the three kingdoms. Ming relations: 'Hokuzan and Nanzan were granted similar commercial status' to Chūzan's 1372 tribute, but only nine missions in about thirty years and no Ming investiture for its kings; a suzerain-side vassal event belongs in the Ming dossier. Amami and Yanbaru are not mentioned on the page. The kings' dates are uncertain on the page itself.
